chapter: Addendum on the Eckstine band arrangers
title: Eckstine arrangers: Valentine, Chippie Alcott, Tadd Dameron and Budd Johnson
summary: He describes the band's writers, with Dameron contributing I Want to Talk About You, Our Delight, Air Mail Special and Good Bait, and Budd Johnson also arranging.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I'll talk about the arrangers. The principal arranger in the band was Jerry Valentine. He did most of the arranging. Another arranger was the trombone player, another trombone player. His name was...well, we called him Chippie Alcott. Chippie before that had played around with... I think when he came to us, he came to us from Tiny Bradshaw's band. Anyway,
Chippie did some of the writing. And I did, of course.

But the other major writer, who joined us about three months after the band had started in 1944, was a very fine arranger -- his name was Tadd Dameron. Tadd was from Cleveland, Ohio, and an arranger with a very unique style of arranging, and was another one of the indelible stamps on the band. While he was with us, one of the things that he wrote was a composition of Billy Eckstine called "I Want To Talk About You." He was the composer of "Our Delight," another up-tempo instrumental that we had. He also made us an arrangement on the the thing that Benny Goodman did, he called it "Good Enough To Keep"...

"Air Mail Special." Which was a Charlie Christian tune. We had a very fine arrangement on that. And while he was with us, one of his pieces that later became a standard was a thing called "Good Bait." And any number of other things that Tadd wrote for the band. In listening to his arrangements and everything, they also made a profound impression on my musicianship as a writer and as a pianist.
